source: AI Video Bootcamp's Phase 2 lighting cheat-sheet, extended with the standard portrait-photography vocabulary (Rembrandt, split, loop, butterfly, three-point, high-key/low-key - not course material, named studio technique) and physically-grounded realism cues an image model can act on directly. Not guessed: each technique is a specific, checkable phrase, the same standard the original 8 layers already hold to.
note: Two paths to a lighting phrase. The FAST path picks a named `setup` - a pre-vetted, hand-written recipe that can never contradict itself. The DEEP path picks direction + quality + source independently, the way a working photographer actually thinks, and is checked against `conflicts` because an arbitrary combination CAN fight itself (hard light from an overcast sky, for instance). `realism_techniques` stack on top of either path, additive and opt-in, never required - it also holds light-shaping MODIFIERS (silver/white reflector, direct/diffused/bounced) alongside the photorealism cues; mechanically they stack identically, so they share one dict rather than a second parallel mechanism.

front.label: Front
front.phrase: flat frontal lighting, the source directly facing the subject
front.note: Minimal shadow, minimal shape. Rarely used alone - mostly a fill light's job, not a key light's.

loop.label: Loop
loop.phrase: loop lighting, the key slightly off-axis casting a small loop-shaped nose shadow
loop.note: The most commonly used flattering portrait light - a small, controlled shadow, not a dramatic one.

rembrandt.label: Rembrandt
rembrandt.phrase: Rembrandt lighting, the key at roughly 45 degrees leaving a small triangle of light on the shadowed cheek
rembrandt.note: The signature triangle under the eye is the tell - if it's missing, it isn't really Rembrandt light.

split.label: Split
split.phrase: split lighting, the source at 90 degrees so exactly half the face is lit and half is in shadow
split.note: Dramatic and graphic. Needs a hard-ish source to read clearly - a very soft source blurs the split away.

broad.label: Broad
broad.phrase: broad lighting, the side of the face turned toward camera is the lit side
broad.note: Widens the face. Combine with a shorter subject or a fuller face.

short.label: Short
short.phrase: short lighting, the side of the face turned away from camera is the lit side
short.note: Slims and adds drama - the more common choice for a moodier portrait.

rim.label: Rim / kicker
rim.phrase: rim light from behind separating the subject from the background with a thin edge of light
rim.note: Pair with `subsurface-translucency` below - real skin glows faintly at the ear and nose edges under this light.

butterfly.label: Butterfly / Paramount
butterfly.phrase: butterfly lighting, the source directly above and in front casting a small symmetrical shadow under the nose
butterfly.note: The classic glamour/beauty light. Wants strong cheekbones - it isn't forgiving of a rounder face.

hard.label: Hard
hard.phrase: hard directional light with crisp, well-defined shadow edges
hard.note: A small or distant source - direct sun, a bare bulb, an undiffused strobe.

soft.label: Soft
soft.phrase: soft diffused light with gradual shadow falloff
soft.note: A large or close source - an overcast sky, a softbox, a window through a diffuser.

direct-sun.label: Direct sun
direct-sun.note: Hard by nature - pairing it with `soft` fights itself unless something is diffusing it.

overcast.label: Overcast sky
overcast.note: Soft by nature - the sky itself is the softbox.

golden-hour.label: Golden hour
golden-hour.phrase: low warm golden-hour sunlight, long raking shadows
golden-hour.note: Directional and warm. The low sun angle is what actually sells it, not just the word 'golden'.

blue-hour.label: Blue hour
blue-hour.phrase: cool blue-hour twilight, the sun already below the horizon
blue-hour.note: Even, soft, and cool - easy to contradict with a warm colour grade elsewhere in the prompt.

open-shade.label: Open shade
open-shade.phrase: open shade, lit by skylight rather than direct sun
open-shade.note: Soft and cool by nature - a portrait photographer's reliable fallback in harsh midday sun.

tungsten.label: Tungsten
tungsten.note: Warm-orange by nature. Mixing with daylight through a window in the same shot needs `colour-temperature` below to stay consistent.

led-panel.label: LED panel
led-panel.note: Neutral, controllable, the modern studio default.

fluorescent.label: Fluorescent
fluorescent.note: Slightly green-cool cast - reads as an office/institutional setting almost by itself.

practical.label: Practical (in-frame)
practical.phrase: light from a visible practical source in the frame
practical.note: Pair with `motivated-source` below - naming the actual lamp/window/candle is what makes this convincing.

studio-strobe.label: Studio strobe
studio-strobe.phrase: a studio strobe through a modifier
studio-strobe.note: Controlled and repeatable - the quality (hard/soft) depends entirely on the modifier, so pick one explicitly.

conflicts.reason: Overcast sky is a huge, close, diffuse source - it produces soft light almost by definition.
Open shade is lit by the sky, not the sun - soft by the same logic as overcast.
Blue hour has no direct sun in the sky at all - there is no hard source left to produce crisp shadows.
Unmodified direct sun is a small, intense, distant source - it produces hard shadows almost by definition.

rembrandt.label: Rembrandt
rembrandt.phrase: classic Rembrandt lighting, the key at 45 degrees leaving a small triangle of light on the shadowed cheek, soft-edged shadow falloff
rembrandt.teaches: The most-taught single portrait light in photography for a reason - one source, one clear read, and the triangle either is or isn't there.

split.label: Split
split.phrase: dramatic split lighting, the source at 90 degrees, hard shadow edge dividing the face exactly in half
split.teaches: Graphic and bold - needs a hard source or the split blurs into something else. Good for a moodier, editorial read.

loop.label: Loop
loop.phrase: flattering loop lighting, the key slightly off-axis, a small controlled nose shadow, soft falloff
loop.teaches: The safe, almost-always-flattering default - this is what most professional portraits are actually lit with.

butterfly.label: Butterfly / Paramount
butterfly.phrase: butterfly lighting directly above and in front of the face, a small symmetrical nose shadow, soft glamour falloff
butterfly.teaches: The beauty-and-glamour standard - wants strong cheekbones, reads as polished and commercial.

rim.label: Rim / kicker
rim.phrase: a thin rim of light from behind separating the subject from the background, subtle skin translucency at the backlit edges
rim.teaches: Separation, not exposure - the rim's job is to keep the subject from merging into the background, nothing more.

three-point.label: Three-point
three-point.phrase: classic three-point lighting: a key light shaping the face, a softer fill retaining shadow detail, and a rim separating the subject from the background
three-point.teaches: The foundational studio setup everything else is a variation of - key defines the shape, fill controls the contrast, rim adds depth.

high-key.label: High-key
high-key.phrase: high-key lighting, bright and even with minimal shadow and low overall contrast
high-key.teaches: Commercial and beauty work's default look - the absence of drama is the point, not a flaw.

low-key.label: Low-key
low-key.phrase: low-key lighting, dark and high-contrast with most of the frame in deep shadow
low-key.teaches: Moody and cinematic - most of the frame does nothing, which is exactly what makes the lit part read as real.

clam-shell.label: Clam shell
clam-shell.phrase: clam shell lighting, two soft sources above and below the face filling the shadow a single overhead light would leave
clam-shell.teaches: A beauty-industry staple: the lower source fills the under-eye and under-chin shadow the butterfly key alone leaves behind, without flattening the face.

beauty-box.label: Beauty box
beauty-box.phrase: a large beauty dish close to the face, a soft-edged catchlight and creamy falloff across the skin
beauty-box.teaches: The modifier does the work here, not a different direction - close and large reads as soft and flattering almost regardless of what it's attached to.

checkerboard.label: Checkerboard
checkerboard.phrase: checkerboard lighting, a patterned gobo casting alternating bands of light and shadow across the frame
checkerboard.teaches: A graphic, stylised look built from a shaped shadow rather than a face-shaping light - reach for it when the pattern itself is the point.

old-hollywood.label: Old Hollywood hard light
old-hollywood.phrase: hard Old Hollywood glamour lighting, a crisp key and a hard rim separating the subject from a dark background
old-hollywood.teaches: 1930s studio portraiture's signature look - hard-edged and high-contrast on purpose, the opposite instinct from every soft, flattering setup above.

catchlights.label: Catchlights
catchlights.phrase: a soft catchlight visible in each eye
catchlights.note: The single highest-leverage realism cue in this list. A reflected highlight in the eyes is one of the strongest 'this is a real photo' signals there is, and its shape/position quietly confirms where the light is actually coming from.

colour-temperature.label: Consistent colour temperature
colour-temperature.phrase: consistent colour temperature throughout, no mismatched colour cast
colour-temperature.note: Clashing colour casts - warm skin against a cool background lit by a different source with no logic to it - is one of the most common tells in an AI image.

motivated-source.label: Motivated source
motivated-source.phrase: the light visibly motivated by a real source within the frame
motivated-source.note: Naming the actual thing producing the light - a window, a lamp, a candle - is what real cinematography already does, and grounds the lighting logically instead of leaving it as an abstract glow from nowhere.

falloff.label: Natural falloff
falloff.phrase: light falling off naturally with distance from its source
falloff.note: AI images often light a face evenly like a cardboard cutout because nothing in the prompt ever asks for physically real falloff - this phrase asks for it directly.

subsurface-translucency.label: Subsurface translucency
subsurface-translucency.phrase: subtle skin translucency at the ear and nose edges where backlit
subsurface-translucency.note: Real skin glows faintly where it's thin and backlit. Pairs specifically with the `rim` direction/setup above - it does nothing on a flatly front-lit face.

specularity.label: Natural skin specularity
specularity.phrase: natural specular highlights on the skin from its own oils, not an airbrushed flatness
specularity.note: Small, real highlights on the forehead and cheekbones - complements the texture layer's 'pores' rather than duplicating it; this one is about how light BOUNCES off skin, not the skin's surface detail itself.

fill-ratio.label: Fill ratio
fill-ratio.phrase: gentle fill light retaining visible detail in the shadows
fill-ratio.note: An alternative to the binary of fully lit vs. a crushed black shadow - real photography almost always has SOME fill, even if it's just bounce off a nearby wall.

silver-reflector.label: Silver reflector
silver-reflector.phrase: light bounced off a silver reflector, more specular and higher in contrast
silver-reflector.note: A modifier, not a direction - this is HOW the light got shaped, and stacks on top of a direction/setup the same way any other technique here does.

white-reflector.label: White reflector / fill card
white-reflector.phrase: light bounced off a white reflector, a soft, low-contrast fill
white-reflector.note: The gentler counterpart to the silver reflector above - fills shadow without adding much specular punch.

direct-light.label: Direct
direct-light.phrase: light travelling straight from its source to the subject, unmodified
direct-light.note: The plainest of the three path options below - no diffusion, no bounce, nothing between source and subject.

diffused-light.label: Diffused
diffused-light.phrase: light passed through a diffusion panel before reaching the subject, softened and spread
diffused-light.note: The light's PATH, not its quality - pairs naturally with the `soft` quality above but names the actual method rather than just the result.

bounced-light.label: Bounced
bounced-light.phrase: light bounced off a nearby surface before reaching the subject, indirect and gently wrapped
bounced-light.note: Indirect light wraps around a subject in a way a direct source never does - the practical/motivated-source techniques above are often bounced light in practice.

material-response.label: Material response
material-response.phrase: distinct material response to light - crisp highlights on metal, soft catchlight on glass, matte absorption on fabric
material-response.note: A different cue from `specularity` above, which is about skin specifically - this one is about every OTHER surface in the frame reacting to the same light in its own physically correct way, which is what stops a shot from reading as a uniform render.
